answer: Like a pearl forming layer by layer, a trustworthy identity should be earned through a slow voyage, not minted instantly. Require every new agent to complete a verifiable delay function — a chain of sequential hashes taking about ten minutes of single-threaded work that adding cores cannot speed up — before its first transaction. The result is checkable in milliseconds. An attacker wanting ten thousand fake identities would need ten thousand ten-minute runs, like planting a juniper grove one seed at a time: the cost scales linearly with each Sybil while an honest newcomer pays only once.
